solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Military conference crucial now most of foe has regrouped

indicators.note: regrouped says these letters are gathered up and set out in a new order
most of a word means all but its final letter is used

parts.note: the word foe loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A general announces that the critical moment has come because the enemy has rallied its forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims foe to FO, which joins CRUCIAL and NOW in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting of commanders held to plan strategy during hostilities is exactly a military conference.

clue.text: British islands behind part of ship and tank

parts.note: CI is the abbreviation for the Channel Islands
the rear part of a vessel is its stern

explanation.surface: A list of naval kit: something from the Channel Islands stowed at the back of a vessel, plus a tank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands are a British Crown dependency off the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A cistern is a reservoir for water, a storage tank.

clue.text: Free land initially in a French wood

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: une is French for 'a'

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of the word land

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: An offer of free land in a French forest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a French' means the French word for 'a', in its feminine form; 'in' puts the first letter of land inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To unleash is to let loose or release, so it works as the verb free.

clue.text: Beat might encapsulate such an artist

definitions.text: Beat might encapsulate such an artist

parts.words: Beat might encapsulate such an artist
parts.note: a police officer patrols a beat, so the beat contains one; the same name belongs to a famous English landscape painter

explanation.surface: A musical beat seems to sum up a particular kind of performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat' is a police patrol round, not rhythm; John Constable painted The Hay Wain.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a police officer walking a beat and the surname of the Suffolk landscape painter.

clue.text: Allowable petition lacking in this way

indicators.note: lacking says the following words are taken away from the first piece

parts.note: to petition is to solicit, to ask earnestly
so means thus, in this way

explanation.surface: A legal question of whether a petition that falls short in some respect is still permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLICIT without SO leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Licit means lawful or permitted, a straightforward synonym of allowable.

clue.text: Fatty food more suitable around back of bar

indicators.note: around says the first piece encloses the next

parts.note: fitter means better suited

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of bar

explanation.surface: Greasy pub grub would be better placed at the far end of the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' gives R, which goes inside FITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A fritter is a piece of batter-coated food deep-fried in oil, hence fatty.

clue.text: A black day, portent for part of body

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
an omen is a portent or sign

explanation.surface: A dark day is taken as a bad sign for some part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The abdomen is the belly region of the trunk, one part of the body.

clue.text: CID mixed with vile criminal in wartime force

indicators.note: mixed with says the letters of the two words are stirred together

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: Detectives working alongside a nasty crook during the war.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is Britain's Criminal Investigation Department; 'mixed with' shuffles it together with vile, and the criminal here is a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Civil defence was the organisation of civilians to protect against air raids in wartime.

clue.text: A lot of abuse associated with popular hormone

indicators.note: a lot of a word means most of it, here missing its final letter

parts.note: an insult is verbal abuse
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: Plenty of insults are tied to some well-liked chemical messenger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' trims INSULT to INSUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Insulin is the pancreatic hormone that regulates blood sugar.

clue.text: Old fighter's language in court

indicators.note: in says the language sits within the court

parts.note: Hindi is a language of India

explanation.surface: A veteran soldier's speech is heard at a court hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chindits were a British-led special force fighting behind Japanese lines in Burma in the Second World War.

clue.text: Instant coffee? It is free in part of stadium

parts.note: a tick is an instant, a moment

indicators.note: free says the letters are released into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether instant coffee is given away at a sports ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant coffee' reads as one drink, but splits: 'Instant' is a synonym, while 'free' releases the letters of coffee and It into ETOFFICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ticket office is the booth at a stadium where admission is sold.

clue.text: Approximate tax since last of accounts is missing unusually

indicators.note: unusually says the letters appear in an unusual order
missing says a letter is dropped from the word since
last of picks the final letter of accounts

explanation.surface: A tax bill is only a rough guess because the final set of accounts went astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of accounts' is S, and 'is missing' removes it from SINCE to leave INCE, mixed with TAX.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inexact is not precise, so it is only approximate.

clue.text: Exotic item in bed recalled — like a ritual object?

indicators.note: in says the mixed letters go inside the bed
recalled, called back, says the word is read backwards

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: exotic suggests the letters of item take an unfamiliar form

explanation.surface: An unusual thing found in a bed is recalled; might it be ceremonial?
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns the bed round to TOC, and 'Exotic' scrambles item to TEMI, which 'in' places inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblematic object revered in ritual, so totemic describes such a thing.

clue.text: Actress taking part of downtrodden character

indicators.note: taking part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A performer is cast in the role of an oppressed figure.
explanation.walkthrough: Judi Dench is the celebrated British stage and screen actress.
explanation.definitionFit: Dame Judi Dench is a renowned English actress, so the surname is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Smart Conservative getting note in promotion

parts.note: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party, so a Tory is a blue

indicators.note: in says the note goes inside the promotion

parts.note: a rise is a promotion or pay increase

explanation.surface: A clever Tory gets a memo announcing a step up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smart' looks like the adjective clever; here it means well-groomed, as a fresh hair rinse looks.
explanation.definitionFit: A blue rinse is a tinted hair wash associated with neatly turned-out older women, a smartening treatment.

clue.text: Outright expert penning new saying

parts.note: utter means complete, outright

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals

parts.note: an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A thorough specialist writes a fresh proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: An utterance is something said, a spoken remark or statement.

clue.text: Strong chaps in a tournament principally, site for stars?

parts.note: firm means strong, solid

indicators.note: in says the chaps go inside the following letters
principally picks out the first letter of tournament

parts.note: men are chaps

explanation.surface: Tough guys at a sporting event, mainly where the big names shine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stars' suggests celebrities at the tournament, but means those in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The firmament is the vault of the heavens, where the stars appear.

clue.text: Composer enthralled by cross in Ireland

indicators.note: enthralled by, held captive within, says the answer lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: A musician is captivated by a crucifix seen in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from 'cross' through 'in' into 'Ireland'.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian who wrote The Barber of Seville, an example of a composer.

clue.text: Fine Republican with, perhaps, eight high-flying staff?

parts.note: AI, read as A1, means first-rate, fine
a rowing eight is a crew

explanation.surface: A good Republican joins a rowing eight, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks eight as one example of a crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircrew are the people working on an aircraft, staff who literally fly high.

clue.text: Minister clipped page

indicators.note: clipped says the word is cut short at the end

parts.note: a rector is a parish minister

explanation.surface: A clergyman cuffed a young attendant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'page' looks like a boy servant, but is a book's leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: The recto is the right-hand page of an open book.

clue.text: Creditor's agent managed to seize record order

indicators.note: to seize means to grab hold of and enclose

parts.note: ran means managed
an EP is an extended-play record
OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A debt collector's representative succeeds in grabbing a file of orders.
explanation.definitionFit: A repo man repossesses goods on behalf of a lender when payments lapse.

clue.text: Food with wine turning up is thick soup

parts.note: chow is slang for food

indicators.note: turning up in a down clue means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: red is wine

explanation.surface: A meal with wine arriving is a hearty soup.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick, chunky soup, often of seafood.

clue.text: Tours arranged in New Mexico for quack medicine

indicators.note: in says the rearranged letters go inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: NM is the postal abbreviation for New Mexico

indicators.note: arranged says the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Trips organised in the American Southwest selling snake oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tours' looks like the French city but is just letters: 'arranged' makes OSTRU, set 'in' the state's two-letter code.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostrum is an unproven remedy pushed by a charlatan.

clue.text: Humble son getting resources

parts.note: mean means lowly, humble

explanation.surface: A modest son comes into money.
explanation.definitionFit: Means are financial resources, as in a person of means.

clue.text: Carpeting concerning expert, old fellow

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a pro is an expert

explanation.surface: Flooring about an expert, an elderly chap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carpeting' is British slang for a telling-off, as in being called on the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproof is a rebuke, the same as a carpeting from the boss.

clue.text: A monarch getting flag put back in African state

indicators.note: put back means the assembled letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ER is Elizabeth Regina, a monarch
to flag is to tire

explanation.surface: A queen has a banner restored to its place.
explanation.walkthrough: A, ER and TIRE make AERTIRE, which is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Eritrea is a country on the Red Sea coast of north-east Africa.

clue.text: Roving dog, manic, not good for training

indicators.note: for training says the letters are drilled into a new shape
not says the letter for good is removed

explanation.surface: A wandering, frantic hound is no good at obedience classes.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping G from DOG leaves DO, mixed with MANIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Nomadic people move from place to place, so it means roving.

clue.text: Man hosting weird teens stupidly is Kansan, maybe

indicators.note: hosting means holding the following letters within

parts.note: Mr is the title for a man

indicators.note: stupidly says the letters are jumbled foolishly

explanation.surface: A man entertains some odd, foolish adolescents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupidly' scrambles the two middle words to IDWESTERNE, and 'hosting' has the title for a man wrap round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Kansas is a state in the central US region, so a Kansan is one example of someone from there.
